The writ petition has been filed in the nature of a Mandamus seeking a direction to the respondent/
Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition Officer) National Highways 209, Dindigul District, to consider a representation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis given by the petitioner dated 28.03.2023.

sentences.text: coconut trees, lemon trees and other fruit yielding trees.
All the trees, are commercial trees.
The respondent had issued a notice seeking to acquire the land in Na.Ka.No. 1179/2022/a3.
The lands of the petitioner are also to be acquired.
The acquisition is for the purpose of forming a Government by-pass road under the National Highways Act, 1956.
The petitioner claims that the trees in his lands should be properly valued and necessary compensation must be given.

3. I am confident that the respondent, while determining the value of the trees, would adhere to the principles as laid down in the Act for valuation of trees and accordingly, the trees would be valued and compensation would be paid.
It is stated by the learned special Government Pleader that this process is on going.
Let the process be completed and let the value of the trees be determined.
If the petitioner is aggrieved, there is always further remedy available in law for the petitioner, to question such valuation of the trees.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.
This Writ Petition stands disposed of.
